messages:
kai: Heads-up, started seeing a sustained tail-latency bump in eu-west for low-priority tenant traffic around 11:04 UTC. p50 fine, p99 up ~3x.

kai: Metric correlates with sudden increase in NIC Tx queue full events on a subset of hosts (see snippet). not a full oom, but GPU kernel stalls.

kai: logs: `host=gpu-az3-07 nic.queue_full=1243 gpu.kernel_retries=18`

infra-bot: Alert: latency-spike detected on cluster=eu-west-2, severity=warning, rule=egress-nic-queuing

jessica: Is this affecting Dedicated pools or shared slices?

kai: Mostly shared fractional slices (soft-isolation). dedicated slices look fine. pattern looks like a small number of tenants doing long seq chat w/ irregular bursts. drives NIC tail and then GPU stalls.

raj: That matches the noisy-ish tenant crosstalk we've seen when egress queues saturate. Two options: 1) punch them to a temporary isolated pool, 2) tweak scheduler scoring to prefer hosts with low NIC backpressure.

olivia: Option 1 reduces latency immediately but increases cost (we'd spin up warm slices). Option 2 is lower cost but needs rollout and tuning.

sam: Quick mitigation: can we temporarily increase preemption aggressiveness for those tenants (bump preempt score) so they get moved off hot hosts?

jessica: Also can we throttle their egress token rate? Might starve the GPU less.

kai: Trying a conservative throttle now for the top-3 offending tenant IDs via internal rate-limiter: `rlctl set tenant-rate tenant:alpha --egress=0.6`

kai: immediate improvement visible on the perf dashboard. p99 dropped ~35% on the affected hosts after ~40s.

raj: Nice. For a medium-term fix I suggest scoring change: add nic_backpressure_i64 to host_score with weight 0.5 and reduce recent_throughput weight. That should route future allocations away from hosts accumulating NIC backpressure.

olivia: We'll need an A/B canary. Keep routing change in soft mode (score bias) then monitor tail-latency and cost.

sam: Cost tradeoff note: moving more workloads to warm isolated slices adds ~12% infra spend for eu-west peak hours. Worth it if it buys p99 SLA headroom.

jessica: Agree — business prefers predictable p99 over the smaller cost delta. But need to avoid thrash/conflicting moves when nodes recover. Add hysteresis.

raj: I'll draft a gating rule: only trigger hard moves if nic.queue_full > 1000 for 2m AND p99 > threshold. Soft-score bias can be enabled at 0.3 immediately.

kai: Action items:
- raj: prepare scheduler scoring PR + unit tests (ETA 6h)
- olivia: run cost impact sim for 24h peak window and post numbers (ETA 3h)
- sam: prepare a runbook snippet to spin warm soft-isolated slices for emergency (ETA 2h)
- jessica: coordinate with support to throttle tenant owners if needed (oncall)

infra-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-3472, severity=warning, assigned=eng-infra

kai: will keep monitoring. tagging @olivia @raj for follow-ups. :eyes:

jessica: Thx — ping if throttle needs to be widened.

raj: PR link when ready — please review fast.

olivia: cost sim looks like +9-14% infra at peak depending on how many tenants we isolate. attaching numbers in tracking doc (link in thread).

kai: closing loop: if score bias + throttles hold p99 within SLA for 30m we'll skip hard pool spin-up. otherwise follow runbook to allocate warm slices.

sam: noted. I'll standby to execute runbook if we cross thresholds. :thumbsup:
